title: Missing middle housing grants and paper bill envelopes
subtitle: Also: inclusionary zoning market update, community engagement policy, HR policies, property tax relief rules and project funding increases.
overview: The committee endorsed in principle a citywide Missing Middle and Affordable Housing Community Improvement Plan. It offers development charge grants for additional dwelling units and larger grants for affordable projects. This was not the statutory public meeting, so the final recommendation returns on December 15, 2025.

The committee also recommended ending return envelopes with mailed paper bills from February 1, 2026 {{vote:m1}}. Supporters pointed to environmental and cost benefits and to e-billing. Another councillor worried about residents who still pay by mail. The committee recommended an updated Community Engagement Policy and consent items on HR policies, property tax relief rules, a hockey academy licence, and funding increases for the Dundee plan and the Ann, Becker and Fife Street project.

The committee received a report on inclusionary zoning with no motion. Staff recommended staying the course for January 2026, while home builders and developers asked for a further pause. A councillor gave notice of a motion for December 15 on lower set-aside rates.

decisions.item: Missing Middle and Affordable Housing CIP
decisions.detail: The committee endorsed in principle a citywide community improvement project area and plan, with agreements delegated to the General Manager of Development Services, pending the December 15 statutory meeting.
The committee recommended discontinuing return envelopes with mailed paper bills effective February 1, 2026, on a recorded vote {{vote:m1}}.
The committee recommended amending the policy to a principles-based approach using the International Association for Public Participation framework.
The committee recommended approving modernized HR policies and repealing redundant ones.

decisions.item: Tax relief for repairs and renovations
decisions.detail: The committee recommended Council approve a draft policy on Municipal Act section 357 applications for repairs and renovations.

decisions.item: Tax relief for sickness or extreme poverty
decisions.detail: The committee recommended a by-law delegating to the Assessment Review Board decisions on eligibility for property tax relief under section 357(1)(d.1).
The committee recommended increasing the Dundee Secondary Plan and Environmental Assessment purchase order by $226,000 including HST.

decisions.item: Ann, Becker and Fife Street inspection contract
decisions.detail: The committee recommended increasing the GHD purchase order for contract administration and inspection by $496,400.34, funded by the Ministry of Transportation and an existing project surplus.

debate: On return envelopes, one councillor worried that residents who pay by mail would be affected and doubted the environmental benefit. Staff said only two of ten comparison municipalities still send envelopes. Supporters called the change fiscally responsible and a nudge toward e-billing.

On the community engagement policy, councillors asked how it would reach underrepresented residents and whether it would add costs. Staff said it is principles-based, requires audience analysis, and has no budget impact now. Statistically valid surveys were described as expensive.

On the housing improvement plan, a councillor questioned whether the affordable rents would suit people experiencing homelessness. Staff said the definition follows the Official Plan and targets low to moderate income households, with many deeper-need projects depending on other governments' funding. Another councillor wanted both grant streams to carry 25-year affordability commitments.
A delegate in support said development charges can decide whether small infill projects proceed, and asked for quick action and clear energy-efficiency criteria.

On inclusionary zoning, home builder and developer delegates said the market is weak and asked for a pause. The consultant said the market cannot currently absorb the policy without financial offsets. Staff and the mayor noted federal funding commitments, and councillors asked who administers the affordable units.
